editorial: When a metallic fragment is fixed to her skull, the film beckons you into a liminal space where danger and desire intertwine. Its genre‑bending formula blends body horror, psychological thriller, and automotive sensuality into a visually intense, almost hypnotic tableau that ridicules conventional narrative arcs. Joaquin Phoenix stays almost mute, delivering every beat with a physicality so visceral that a single glance at the screen feels like a punch. Still, a dragging middle act thins the impact, making the frantic rhythm of the opening feel a touch lurching. If you thrive on cinema that demands attention to detail and the willingness to let your appetite for the uncanny run wild, this work will keep you company.
targetAudience: Ideal for viewers craving visceral, cerebral cinema with unsettling body horror.
